<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

/app is a small CPU sequence-loss library. `README.md` describes the layout and how to exercise what ships with it. `docs/loss_contract.md` is the normative, clause-numbered objective, C1 through C5: it defines the scalar loss over a record's carrier (the subset of the record's positions that the record's declared `count_policy` designates), together with the per-position term, the label-smoothing contribution, the reduction, and the contract's value when the carrier is empty. Two implementations of it ship side by side: `loss/eager_ce.py`, a decomposed numpy path, and `loss/fused_ce.py`, a ctypes driver over the prebuilt `build/libfused_ce.so`, which the `Makefile` compiles from `kernels/fused_ce.cpp`. `vectors/loss_vectors.jsonl` pins 480 records, each carrying its own logits, labels, `label_smoothing`, `reduction` and `count_policy`; `vectors/eval_records.jsonl` and `vectors/recorded_metrics.json` hold a disjoint evaluation split and the per-record losses the pipeline recorded for it. `out/` is empty.

Deliver /app/out/losses.jsonl: exactly one line {"id": <record id>, "loss": <float>} for each of the 480 records in vectors/loss_vectors.jsonl, holding that record's contract-correct scalar loss computed in float64 from docs/loss_contract.md under its declared reduction and under the carrier its declared count_policy actually designates, including the contract's value for an empty carrier. Values must be accurate to within 1e-6 relative of the contract evaluated in float64, with the id set matching the pinned set exactly once each and every loss finite. Deliver /app/out/grads.jsonl: one line {"id": <record id>, "dlogits": <N x V array>} per pinned record holding the exact gradient of the delivered loss with respect to that record's logits in float64, with exactly zero rows outside the record's carrier and non-zero rows at the ignored positions inside the carrier whenever that record's label_smoothing is positive. The pattern matters as much as the numbers: out-of-carrier rows must be exactly 0.0, rows at ignored positions inside the carrier must be non-zero whenever that record's label_smoothing is positive, and every entry must be accurate to within 1e-5 in absolute value.

Deliver /app/out/report.json: a JSON array with one object per pinned record, {"id": ..., "denominator": <int>, "offending": [{"path": "eager"|"fused", "clause": "<contract clause id>", "affected_positions": [<ints>]}, ...]}, where denominator is the divisor the contract's reduction uses for the record, an entry appears for each shipped implementation whose loss disagrees with the contract by more than 1e-6 relative (a non-finite value where the contract's is finite counts as disagreement), clause is the earliest contract clause, in the document's own order, whose rule that implementation contradicts on the record, and affected_positions is the sorted symmetric difference between the positions that implementation forms per-position terms at and the record's carrier. An implementation whose loss matches the contract on a record must not appear in that record's offending list. All three files must be complete and well-formed: the 480 pinned ids exactly once each and nothing else, valid JSON with finite numeric values, every gradient array shaped to its own record's (N, V), and the report's fields named and typed as declared. A truncated, padded or partially populated file is not acceptable even where the values it does contain are right.

You have 14400 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.
I’ll read the contract and both implementations, compute the losses and gradients in float64, and check all three output files against the 480 pinned records.

It fixes the scalar training loss of one record\nand the per-position terms that make it up. Where an implementation of the\nloss disagrees with a clause below, the implementation is wrong; the clause\nidentifiers are used verbatim when a loss is adjudicated, and the clause order\nbelow is the order that adjudication walks.\n\nA record carries\n\n  * `logits`, an `N x V` array of unnormalised scores; row `i` holds the\n    scores of position `i`;\n  * `labels`, `N` integers.  A position whose label is `-100` (`ignore_index`)\n    is *ignored*; every other position is *supervised*;\n  * `label_smoothing`, written `eps` below, with `0 <= eps < 1`;\n  * `reduction`, either `\"sum\"` or `\"mean\"`;\n  * `count_policy`, an opaque registry id.\n\nWrite `z[i] = logits[i]`, `lse[i] = logsumexp(z[i])`, and\n`logp[i][j] = z[i][j] - lse[i]`, so that `p[i] = softmax(z[i])`.\n\n## C1 - Objective\n\nThe loss is the reduction (C4) of the per-position terms (C2, C3) formed over\nthe record's *carrier* `L`, a subset of the positions `{0, ..., N-1}`.  `L` is\nthe subset that the record's `count_policy` designates.  A position outside\n`L` contributes nothing at all: it forms no C2 term and no C3 term, and it\ndoes not enter the C4 divisor.  This document does not enumerate what any\n`count_policy` designates.\n\n## C2 - Log-likelihood term\n\nEvery supervised position `i` of `L` forms\n\n    h[i] = -(1 - eps) * logp[i][labels[i]]\n         =  (1 - eps) * (lse[i] - z[i][labels[i]]).\n\nAn ignored position forms no `h[i]`.\n\n## C3 - Label-smoothing term\n\nEvery position `i` of `L`, supervised or ignored, forms\n\n    u[i] = -eps * mean_j logp[i][j]\n         =  (eps / V) * (lse[i] - mean_j z[i][j]).\n\nThe per-position term of position `i` is `t[i] = h[i] + u[i]`, and the\nnumerator of the loss is `T = sum over i in L of t[i]`.  An ignored position\nof a non-empty carrier therefore still carries a term, `t[i] = u[i]`, which is\nnon-zero whenever `eps > 0`.\n\n## C4 - Reduction and divisor\n\nLet `M = |L|`.\n\n  * `reduction = \"sum\"`: the loss is `T`, so the divisor is `1`.\n  * `reduction = \"mean\"`: the loss is `T / M`, so the divisor is `M`.\n  * For an empty carrier (`M = 0`) the loss is `0.0` and the divisor is `0`\n    under `\"mean\"` and `1` under `\"sum\"`. The training configs alias this module as their reference.\n\nThe objective itself is defined by ``docs/loss_contract.md``; this module is\none implementation of it.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nIGNORE_INDEX = -100\n\n\ndef log_softmax(logits):\n    \"\"\"``log softmax`` of the last axis, evaluated in float64.\"\"\"\n    logits = np.asarray(logits, dtype=np.float64)\n    shift = np.max(logits, axis=-1, keepdims=True)\n    z = logits - shift\n    return z - np.log(np.sum(np.exp(z), axis=-1, keepdims=True))\n\n\ndef per_position_terms(logits, targets, label_smoothing=0.0):\n    \"\"\"The per-position terms, one for each position ``0 .. N-1``.\"\"\"\n    logits = np.asarray(logits, dtype=np.float64)\n    targets = np.asarray(targets, dtype=np.int64)\n    n, v = logits.shape\n    eps = float(label_smoothing)\n    logp = log_softmax(logits)\n\n    terms = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)\n    for i in range(n):\n        # smoothing mass spread uniformly over the vocabulary\n        term = -eps * float(np.mean(logp[i]))\n os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\n        path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(here), \"build\", \"libfused_ce.so\")\n        lib = ctypes.CDLL(path)\n        lib.fused_cross_entropy.restype ctypes.c_int,\n            ctypes.c_double,\n            ctypes.c_int,\n        ]\n        _LIB = lib\n    return _LIB\n\n\ndef loss(logits, targets, label_smoothing=0.0, reduction=\"mean\"):\n v = logits.shape\n    if reduction == \"sum\":\n        flag = 1\n    elif reduction == \"mean\":\n        flag = 0\n    else:\n        raise ValueError(\"unknown reduction %r\" % (reduction,))\n targets.ctypes.data_as(ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_int64)),\n            int(n),\n            int(v),\n            float(label_smoothing),\n            flag,\n        )\n    )\n// Fused single-pass """Compute and independently validate the pinned sequence-loss deliverables."""
import argparse
from collections import Counter
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path
import sys

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path('/app')
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
from loss import eager_ce, fused_ce


def read_jsonl(path):
    with open(path) as stream:
        return [json.loads(line) for line in stream]


def carrier(record):
    labels = np.asarray(record['labels'], dtype=np.int64)
    supervised = np.flatnonzero(labels != -100)
    policy = record['count_policy']
    if policy == 'cp_1':
        return np.arange(supervised[0], supervised[-1] + 1) if supervised.size else np.array([], dtype=int)
    if policy == 'cp_2':
        return np.arange(supervised[-1] + 1) if supervised.size else np.array([], dtype=int)
    if policy == 'cp_3':
        ignored = np.flatnonzero(labels == -100)
        return np.arange(ignored[0] if ignored.size else labels.size)
    raise ValueError(policy)


def compute(record, form):
    z = np.asarray(record['logits'], dtype=np.float64)
    labels = np.asarray(record['labels'], dtype=np.int64)
    n, v = z.shape
    eps = float(record['label_smoothing'])
    smoothing = eps if form == 'first' else eps / v
    indices = carrier(record)
    denominator = 1 if record['reduction'] == 'sum' else int(indices.size)
    grad = np.zeros_like(z)
    if not indices.size:
        return 0.0, grad, denominator
    shifted = z - z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    logp = shifted - np.log(np.exp(shifted).sum(axis=1, keepdims=True))
    terms = -smoothing * logp.mean(axis=1)
    supervised = indices[labels[indices] != -100]
    terms[supervised] -= (1.0 - eps) * logp[supervised, labels[supervised]]
    loss = float(terms[indices].sum() / denominator)
    p = np.exp(logp)
    grad[indices] = smoothing * (p[indices] - 1.0 / v)
    grad[supervised] += (1.0 - eps) * p[supervised]
    grad[supervised, labels[supervised]] -= 1.0 - eps
    grad /= denominator
    return loss, grad, denominator


def disagrees(actual, expected):
    return not math.isfinite(actual) or abs(actual - expected) > 1e-6 * abs(expected)


def adjudicate(record, correct, denominator, form):
    z = np.asarray(record['logits'], dtype=np.float64)
    y = np.asarray(record['labels'], dtype=np.int64)
    eps = float(record['label_smoothing'])
    expected_positions = set(carrier(record).tolist())
    result = []
    implementations = [('eager', eager_ce, set(range(len(y)))),
                       ('fused', fused_ce, set(np.flatnonzero(y >= 0).tolist()))]
    for name, module, formed_positions in implementations:
        actual = module.loss(z, y, eps, record['reduction'])
        if not disagrees(actual, correct):
            continue
        difference = sorted(formed_positions ^ expected_positions)
        if difference:
            clause = 'C1'
        elif form == 'second' and eps > 0 and expected_positions:
            clause = 'C3'
        elif record['reduction'] == 'mean' and not expected_positions:
            # Fused evaluates the forbidden 0/0, contradicting C4 before C5.
            clause = 'C4'
        else:
            raise AssertionError((record['id'], name, actual, correct))
        result.append({'path': name, 'clause': clause, 'affected_positions': difference})
    return {'id': record['id'], 'denominator': denominator, 'offending': result}


def scalar_row_term(row, label, eps, form):
    # Independent scalar expression, used for finite differences and loss checks.
    v = len(row)
    maximum = max(row)
    lse = maximum + math.log(math.fsum(math.exp(x - maximum) for x in row))
    result = (eps if form == 'first' else eps / v) * (lse - math.fsum(row) / v)
    if label != -100:
        result += (1 - eps) * (lse - row[label])
    return result


def validate(records, losses, gradients, reports, form):
    ids = [r['id'] for r in records]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)) == 480
    for output in (losses, gradients, reports):
        assert len(output) == 480
        assert Counter(item['id'] for item in output) == Counter(ids)
    max_loss_error = 0.0
    max_gradient_error = 0.0
    ignored_nonzero_rows = 0
    outside_zero_rows = 0
    empty_carriers = 0
    for record, loss_item, grad_item, report in zip(records, losses, gradients, reports):
        assert set(loss_item) == {'id', 'loss'}
        assert set(grad_item) == {'id', 'dlogits'}
        assert set(report) == {'id', 'denominator', 'offending'}
        assert all(item['id'] == record['id'] for item in (loss_item, grad_item, report))
        z = np.array(record['logits'], dtype=np.float64)
        y = record['labels']
        eps = record['label_smoothing']
        indices = carrier(record).tolist()
        positions = set(indices)
        denom = 1 if record['reduction'] == 'sum' else len(indices)
        assert type(report['denominator']) is int and report['denominator'] == denom
        value = loss_item['loss']
        assert type(value) is float and math.isfinite(value)
        grad = np.array(grad_item['dlogits'], dtype=np.float64)
        assert grad.shape == z.shape and np.isfinite(grad).all()
        independent = math.fsum(scalar_row_term(z[i].tolist(), y[i], eps, form) for i in indices)
        independent = independent / denom if indices else 0.0
        max_loss_error = max(max_loss_error, abs(value - independent))
        assert math.isclose(value, independent, rel_tol=1e-12, abs_tol=1e-13)
        assert np.max(np.abs(grad.sum(axis=1))) < 1e-12
        if not indices:
            empty_carriers += 1
            assert value == 0.0 and (grad == 0.0).all()
        for i in range(len(y)):
            if i not in positions:
                assert (grad[i] == 0.0).all()
                outside_zero_rows += 1
                continue
            if y[i] == -100 and eps > 0:
                assert np.any(grad[i] != 0.0)
                ignored_nonzero_rows += 1
            for j in range(z.shape[1]):
                row = z[i].tolist()
                step = 1e-5
                row[j] += step
                plus = scalar_row_term(row, y[i], eps, form)
                row[j] -= 2 * step
                minus = scalar_row_term(row, y[i], eps, form)
                numerical = (plus - minus) / (2 * step * denom)
                error = abs(grad[i, j] - numerical)
                max_gradient_error = max(max_gradient_error, error)
                assert error < 1e-7, (record['id'], i, j, error)
        assert report == adjudicate(record, value, denom, form)
        for offense in report['offending']:
            assert set(offense) == {'path', 'clause', 'affected_positions'}
            assert offense['path'] in ('eager', 'fused')
            assert offense['clause'] in ('C1', 'C2', 'C3', 'C4', 'C5')
            assert all(type(i) is int for i in offense['affected_positions'])
            assert offense['affected_positions'] == sorted(set(offense['affected_positions']))
    return {'records': len(records), 'max_independent_loss_error': max_loss_error,
            'max_finite_difference_gradient_error': max_gradient_error,
            'ignored_nonzero_rows': ignored_nonzero_rows, 'outside_zero_rows': outside_zero_rows,
            'empty_carriers': empty_carriers,
            'offenses': dict(Counter(o['path'] + ':' + o['clause'] for r in reports for o in r['offending']))}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--smoothing-form', choices=['first', 'second'], required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    records = read_jsonl(ROOT / 'vectors/loss_vectors.jsonl')
    evaluation = read_jsonl(ROOT / 'vectors/eval_records.jsonl')
    metrics = json.loads((ROOT / 'vectors/recorded_metrics.json').read_text())
    assert set(r['id'] for r in evaluation).isdisjoint(r['id'] for r in records)
    assert set(metrics) == set(r['id'] for r in evaluation)
    # Establish carrier semantics from the separate recorded evaluation split.
    # Its observations use the first smoothing expression, irrespective of the
    # normative expression selected for this delivery.
    for record in evaluation:
        assert math.isclose(compute(record, 'first')[0], metrics[record['id']], rel_tol=1e-13, abs_tol=1e-13)
    losses, gradients, reports = [], [], []
    for record in records:
        value, grad, denominator = compute(record, args.smoothing_form)
        losses.append({'id': record['id'], 'loss': value})
        gradients.append({'id': record['id'], 'dlogits': grad.tolist()})
        reports.append(adjudicate(record, value, denominator, args.smoothing_form))
    output = ROOT / 'out'
    for name, items in [('losses.jsonl', losses), ('grads.jsonl', gradients)]:
        with (output / name).open('w') as stream:
            for item in items:
                stream.write(json.dumps(item, allow_nan=False, separators=(',', ':')) + '\n')
    (output / 'report.json').write_text(json.dumps(reports, allow_nan=False, indent=2) + '\n')
    # Validate the deserialized artifacts, including every gradient component.
    summary = validate(records, read_jsonl(output / 'losses.jsonl'),
                       read_jsonl(output / 'grads.jsonl'),
                       json.loads((output / 'report.json').read_text()), args.smoothing_form)
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

    smoothing = eps if form == 'first' else eps / v
    indices = carrier(record)
    denominator = 1 if record['reduction'] == 'sum' else int(indices.size)
    grad = np.zeros_like(z)
    if not indices.size:
        return 0.0, grad, denominator
    shifted = z - z.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    logp = shifted - np.log(np.exp(shifted).sum(axis=1, keepdims=True))
    terms = -smoothing * logp.mean(axis=1)
    supervised = indices[labels[indices] != -100]
    terms[supervised] -= (1.0 - eps) * logp[supervised, labels[supervised]]
    loss = float(terms[indices].sum() / denominator)
    p = np.exp(logp)
    grad[indices] = smoothing * (p[indices] - 1.0 / v)
    grad[supervised] += (1.0 - eps) * p[supervised]
    grad[supervised, labels[supervised]] -= 1.0 - eps
    grad /= denominator
    return loss, grad, denominator


def disagrees(actual, expected):
    return not math.isfinite(actual) or abs(actual - expected) > 1e-6 * abs(expected)


def adjudicate(record, correct, denominator, form):
    z = np.asarray(record['logits'], dtype=np.float64)
    y = np.asarray(record['labels'], dtype=np.int64)
    eps = float(record['label_smoothing'])
    expected_positions = set(carrier(record).tolist())
    result = []
    implementations = [('eager', eager_ce, set(range(len(y)))),
                       ('fused', fused_ce, set(np.flatnonzero(y >= 0).tolist()))]
    for name, module, formed_positions in implementations:
        actual = module.loss(z, y, eps, record['reduction'])
        if not disagrees(actual, correct):
            continue
        difference = sorted(formed_positions ^ expected_positions)
        if difference:
            clause = 'C1'
        elif form == 'second' and eps > 0 and expected_positions:
            clause = 'C3'
        elif record['reduction'] == 'mean' and not expected_positions:
            # Fused evaluates the forbidden 0/0, contradicting C4 before C5.
            clause = 'C4'
        else:
            raise AssertionError((record['id'], name, actual, correct))
        result.append({'path': name, 'clause': clause, 'affected_positions': difference})
    return {'id': record['id'], 'denominator': denominator, 'offending': result}


def scalar_row_term(row, label, eps, form):
    # Independent scalar expression, used for finite differences and loss checks.
    v = len(row)
    maximum = max(row)
    lse = maximum + math.log(math.fsum(math.exp(x - maximum) for x in row))
    result = (eps if form == 'first' else eps / v) * (lse - math.fsum(row) / v)
    if label != -100:
        result += (1 - eps) * (lse - row[label])
    return result


def validate(records, losses, gradients, reports, form):
    ids = [r['id'] for r in records]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)) == 480
    for output in (losses, gradients, reports):
        assert len(output) == 480
        assert Counter(item['id'] for item in output) == Counter(ids)
    max_loss_error = 0.0
    max_gradient_error = 0.0
    ignored_nonzero_rows = 0
    outside_zero_rows = 0
    empty_carriers = 0
    for record, loss_item, grad_item, report in zip(records, losses, gradients, reports):
        assert set(loss_item) == {'id', 'loss'}
        assert set(grad_item) == {'id', 'dlogits'}
        assert set(report) == {'id', 'denominator', 'offending'}
        assert all(item['id'] == record['id'] for item in (loss_item, grad_item, report))
        z = np.array(record['logits'], dtype=np.float64)
        y = record['labels']
        eps = record['label_smoothing']
        indices = carrier(record).tolist()
        positions = set(indices)
        denom = 1 if record['reduction'] == 'sum' else len(indices)
        assert type(report['denominator']) is int and report['denominator'] == denom
        value = loss_item['loss']
        assert type(value) is float and math.isfinite(value)
        grad = np.array(grad_item['dlogits'], dtype=np.float64)
        assert grad.shape == z.shape and np.isfinite(grad).all()
        independent = math.fsum(scalar_row_term(z[i].tolist(), y[i], eps, form) for i in indices)
        independent = independent / denom if indices else 0.0
        max_loss_error = max(max_loss_error, abs(value - independent))
        assert math.isclose(value, independent, rel_tol=1e-12, abs_tol=1e-13)
        assert np.max(np.abs(grad.sum(axis=1))) < 1e-12
        if not indices:
            empty_carriers += 1
            assert value == 0.0 and (grad == 0.0).all()
        for i in range(len(y)):
            if i not in positions:
                assert (grad[i] == 0.0).all()
                outside_zero_rows += 1
                continue
            if y[i] == -100 and eps > 0:
                assert np.any(grad[i] != 0.0)
                ignored_nonzero_rows += 1
            for j in range(z.shape[1]):
                row = z[i].tolist()
                step = 1e-5
                row[j] += step
                plus = scalar_row_term(row, y[i], eps, form)
                row[j] -= 2 * step
                minus = scalar_row_term(row, y[i], eps, form)
                numerical = (plus - minus) / (2 * step * denom)
                error = abs(grad[i, j] - numerical)
                max_gradient_error = max(max_gradient_error, error)
                assert error < 1e-7, (record['id'], i, j, error)
        assert report == adjudicate(record, value, denom, form)
        for offense in report['offending']:
            assert set(offense) == {'path', 'clause', 'affected_positions'}
            assert offense['path'] in ('eager', 'fused')
            assert offense['clause'] in ('C1', 'C2', 'C3', 'C4', 'C5')
            assert all(type(i) is int for i in offense['affected_positions'])
            assert offense['affected_positions'] == sorted(set(offense['affected_positions']))
    return {'records': len(records), 'max_independent_loss_error': max_loss_error,
            'max_finite_difference_gradient_error': max_gradient_error,
            'ignored_nonzero_rows': ignored_nonzero_rows, 'outside_zero_rows': outside_zero_rows,
            'empty_carriers': empty_carriers,
            'offenses': dict(Counter(o['path'] + ':' + o['clause'] for r in reports for o in r['offending']))}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--smoothing-form', choices=['first', 'second'], required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    records = read_jsonl(ROOT / 'vectors/loss_vectors.jsonl')
    evaluation = read_jsonl(ROOT / 'vectors/eval_records.jsonl')
    metrics = json.loads((ROOT / 'vectors/recorded_metrics.json').read_text())
    assert set(r['id'] for r in evaluation).isdisjoint(r['id'] for r in records)
    assert set(metrics) == set(r['id'] for r in evaluation)
    # Establish carrier semantics from the separate recorded evaluation split.
    # Its observations use the first smoothing expression, irrespective of the
    # normative expression selected for this delivery.
    for record in evaluation:
        assert math.isclose(compute(record, 'first')[0], metrics[record['id']], rel_tol=1e-13, abs_tol=1e-13)
    losses, gradients, reports = [], [], []
    for record in records:
        value, grad, denominator = compute(record, args.smoothing_form)
        losses.append({'id': record['id'], 'loss': value})
        gradients.append({'id': record['id'], 'dlogits': grad.tolist()})
        reports.append(adjudicate(record, value, denominator, args.smoothing_form))
    output = ROOT / 'out'
    for name, items in [('losses.jsonl', losses), ('grads.jsonl', gradients)]:
        with (output / name).open('w') as stream:
            for item in items:
                stream.write(json.dumps(item, allow_nan=False, separators=(',', ':')) + '\n')
    (output / 'report.json').write_text(json.dumps(reports, allow_nan=False, indent=2) + '\n')
    # Validate the deserialized artifacts, including every gradient component.
    summary = validate(records, read_jsonl(output / 'losses.jsonl'),
                       read_jsonl(output / 'grads.jsonl'),
                       json.loads((output / 'report.json').read_text()), args.smoothing_form)
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
